info.name: Customer Management API v2
info.description:
Two APIs in one collection.

**Mobile App API**: the only endpoints the mobile app may call.
**Internal API (not for mobile)**: health probes, staff operations, sync jobs and provider webhooks.

Set `baseUrl`, `internalUrl`, `astppToken` and `astppId`. Each request's Tests tab captures tokens and ids into collection variables, so later requests just work. First-time order: Wallet > Get wallet onboarding status, Authentication > Sign in: New device (registers device, starts wallet creation), Authentication > Confirm wallet verification code, PIN > Set the initial PIN (optional -- balance/transactions need it, everything else doesn't).

item.name: Wallet

item.name: Authentication
item.description: Sessions and tokens. Registering a new device and creating its wallet happens here too (see "Sign in: New device"), since the mobile app only ever experiences it as signing in -- wallet creation is a backend detail.

item.name: Sign in: New device (registers device, starts wallet creation)

header.description: Required ASTPP encrypted token for this account

request.description:
The one sign-in endpoint. What it needs depends on the customer and the phone:

| Situation | Send | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Brand-new device -- no device/wallet registered yet (this request) | `astpp_id` + `device` | `201` tokens, plus `walletStatus` and `pinSet` so the app knows what to do next |
| Phone already verified for this customer | `pin` + `device` | `201` tokens |
| New phone, reinstall or cleared data | `pin` + `idNumber` + `device` | `202` OTP challenge, then `POST /api/v2/auth/sessions/{sessionId}/otp-verifications` |

This branch is what used to be two separate calls (`POST /wallets` to register the device and create the wallet, then `POST /auth/sessions` to sign in). They are merged here because the device/customer has no idea a wallet is being created for them behind the scenes -- it's purely a backend/PSP (SasaPay) concern, so it belongs with sign-in, not with a `wallets` resource the app doesn't otherwise touch until the wallet exists.

`astpp_id` **is** required on this branch specifically (it wasn't on the old first-sign-in call) because nothing has been validated for this device yet. On every other branch it's still not needed, since the device was already registered here.

What happens on success: the device row is created, a background job sends the customer's profile to SasaPay to create the wallet, and the customer is signed in immediately -- `201` with an access token, refresh token and `sessionId`, **even though the wallet itself is still `pending_otp`**. The app can go straight to the wallet home screen shell; `walletStatus` and `pinSet` in the response tell it what to overlay:
- `walletStatus: "pending_otp"` -> prompt for the SMS code SasaPay just sent, then call `POST /api/v2/auth/wallet-verifications?astppId={astppId}`.
- `pinSet: false` -> the customer can use the app, but balance and transaction endpoints stay locked until `POST /customers/me/pin` is called, because those require a PIN-scoped (transaction) token, not just `app:access`.

Idempotent: send the same `Idempotency-Key` on a retry after a timeout so the device/wallet aren't created twice; a retry with a device that's already registered still returns `201` with a fresh session.

**If the SMS code expires (or all attempts are used) before it's confirmed:** the wallet is still not created on SasaPay's side, so the customer isn't fully onboarded. Call this same endpoint again with the same `Idempotency-Key` pattern to start a new PSP job and get a new code. *Open question, not yet confirmed with backend: whether `device` needs to be resent on that retry, or whether `astpp_id` alone is enough once the device row already exists -- flagging this rather than guessing.*

A `202` (other branches) creates a session in a *pending* state. Its id is the id you later see in `/customers/me/sessions`.

If `device_identifier` already belongs to a different device on this account (model/OS changed without going through a proper re-registration), the answer is `409 DEVICE_MISMATCH` with an `errors[]` entry naming the mismatched field and both the `expected` (currently registered) and `actual` (submitted) values -- e.g. `device.device_model`.

header.description: Required ASTPP encrypted token for this account

request.description:
The one sign-in endpoint. What it needs depends on the customer and the phone:

| Situation | Send | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Customer has no PIN yet (first install) | `device` only | `201` tokens |
| Phone already verified for this customer | `pin` + `device` | `201` tokens |
| New phone, reinstall or cleared data | `pin` + `idNumber` + `device` | `202` OTP challenge, then `POST /api/v2/auth/sessions/{sessionId}/otp-verifications` |

The server decides whether a phone is "verified" (a verified session exists for the same `device_identifier`
in the last 90 days). If the phone is new and `idNumber` is missing the answer is `422 ID_NUMBER_REQUIRED`,
returned **before** the PIN is checked, so it never reveals whether the PIN was right. `astpp_id` is not
needed here - it was already validated once, when the device was registered.

A `202` creates a session in a *pending* state. Its id is the id you later see in `/customers/me/sessions`.
